newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel unveils corporate disclosure proposal.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel unveils corporate disclosure proposal.

text.p: An advisory body to Japan's finance minister, the Business Accounting Council, unveiled on Friday its draft proposals to improve Japan's corporate earnings disclosure.
A key member of the advisory panel, Tetsuya Morita, said the proposals are aimed at harmonising domestic disclosure practices with international standards.

He said that it would be necessary to change the nation's disclosure practices, which presently put priority on parent-only earnings. In the United States, corporate earnings are all released on a consolidated basis.

Under the draft proposals, companies will have to disclose all of their group earnings if parent companies are involved in the management of a subsidiary. Current rules require corporations to disclose the financial statement of a subsidiary only if 50 percent or more of the unit's shares are owned by the parent firm.

Companies would also be asked to announce interim financial statements based on a consolidated basis. Current rules require companies to announce parent interim and annual statements and only annual group statements.
